title: Field Deploy Resiliency Cheat Sheet — hybrid on-prem + vSphere (terraform module notes)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, field-facing cheat sheet for resilient on-prem Kubernetes deploys that mix bare-metal and vSphere hosts. It focuses on the common pain points we see during initial cluster bootstrap, cold-start behaviour, network fabric fallbacks, and the minimum Terraform module surface we need to support robust upgrades and rollback.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs, site ops, and solutions engineers doing customer on-prem or VPC-connected installs.
- Scope: cluster bootstrap (control plane + initial workers), day-0 networking quirks, Terraform module interfaces and upgrade plan (0.0 -> 1.x), and short runbook for rollback and telemetry checks. Not a full runbook for app migrations.

Assumptions (implicit):
- Customer has a mix of: dedicated bare-metal racks (PXE or image service) + vSphere guests for worker or edge pools.
- Out-of-band BMC access exists (iDRAC/ipmi/ILO) for at least one node in each rack.
- A private registry / offline artifacts may be required in air-gapped sites.
- We use our standard control plane layout: 3 control-plane nodes (HA), etcd on control plane, and worker pools split by hardware class.

Quick wins / golden rules (short):
1) Always validate physical network MTU end-to-end before bootstrap. Use: iperf3 or ping -M do -s 1472 <peer>.
2) Ensure L2/L3 paths for Kubernetes service CIDR and pod CIDR are routable between control plane and workers (and between racks).
3) Bring up a minimal control plane on a stable VLAN first; add worker pools after control plane and CNI healthchecks pass.
4) Add gateway fallback routes for pod/service CIDRs in case top-of-rack ARP tables flake.
5) Use one Terraform plan per logical plane: control-plane, worker-pools, infra-services (load-balancers, registry, DNS).

Preflight checklist (quick, executable):
- [ ] Inventory servers and firmware versions (iDRAC/Firmware) — known bad combos: Broadcom NIC offloads + old firmware => ARP flapping on vSwitch.
- [ ] BMC access confirmed and credentials staged in vault.
- [ ] IPMI/iDRAC test: power cycle a test host remotely.
- [ ] DNS resolution for control plane fqdn from each worker subnet.
- [ ] Private registry reachable (or registry image mirror configured).
- [ ] NTP reachability and clock skew < 300ms across nodes.
- [ ] MTU validated across fabric for requested pod MTU (e.g., 1500 vs 9000).

Network fallback patterns (common issues + mitigations):
- Symptom: intermittent pod -> pod across racks fails after scale.
  Root causes: switch ASIC offload bug, incorrect MTU, vSphere promiscuous mode disabled on vSwitch.
  Mitigation: force MTU downward on physical interfaces (temporary), enable promiscuous/all forged transmits on vSwitch during rollout, and route cluster CIDR through explicit static routes on top-of-rack for a canary rack.

- Symptom: Node becomes NotReady during large pod startup (KV backend pressure).
  Root causes: CPU saturation on iSCSI/bonding driver, CNI heavy packet copying.
  Mitigation: increase kubelet eviction thresholds temporarily, throttle pod parallelism in daemonset rolling updates, add dedicated NIC path for pod traffic.

Control plane bootstrap sequence (recommended minimal order):
1) Deploy control-plane TF stack: core-vlan, control-plane VMs/hosts, IP assignments, base DNS entries.
2) Provision base OS image and essential packages (container runtime, cri tools).
3) Bootstrap k8s control-plane (kubeadm/rendered manifests) on 1 node; verify etcd, apiserver, controller-manager.
4) Join CP2/CP3. Wait for etcd cluster healthy (etcdctl endpoint status).
5) Deploy local registry + internal DNS + CNI (calico/cilium) minimal config.
6) Run CNI sanity tests (can serve DNS, pod ping to control-plane pod IP).
7) Add worker pools via TF and join nodes; label pools (baremetal/fast-gpu/vsphere).
8) Deploy core infra (metrics-server, kube-proxy, ingress-native LB / metallb).

Terraform module notes (interface and expectations):
- Module split (recommended):
  - module/control_plane (inputs: cluster_name, control_plane_count, cp_hostnames[], cp_network_map, k8s_version, certs_location)
  - module/worker_pool (inputs: pool_name, count, flavor, boot_method, network_id, labels, taints, mount_profiles)
  - module/infra_services (inputs: registry_image_mirror, metallb_ranges, dns_zone, ntp_servers)
  - module/bootscripts (inputs: image_url, ignition_config, user_data_template)
- Minimal outputs from modules (we rely on these):
  - control_plane: apiserver_endpoint, control_plane_ips (csv), etcd_endpoints
  - worker_pool: worker_ips[], pool_tags (for inventory)
  - infra_services: registry_endpoint, metallb_allocations
- Important variable semantics (avoid breaking changes):
  - Never change control_plane_count without a coordinated plan; modules should expose a boolean "allow_cp_count_change" to gate accidental reduces.
  - bootscripts should be idempotent and keyed by revision hash; module should expose last_applied_boot_hash to detect drift.

Upgrade plan template (kubernetes minor/patch upgrades):
Phases: canary -> staged -> full.
- Canary: upgrade 1 worker in each pool and 1 control-plane node (if cp minor update is required). Validate for 2x deploy windows (or 48h depending on customer).
- Staged: upgrade 25% of worker nodes in each pool, monitor infra metrics for 1h.
- Full: remaining nodes in waves of 30% per wave.

Validation checks after each phase (automatable):
- kube-apiserver metrics: request_latencies 95th not increased > 30%
- etcd health: quorum count consistent; 10s average commit time not increased > 2x
- Pod readiness rate: >= 99% within 5 minutes of rolling a DaemonSet update
- E2E smoke: run 50 simple request flows to the app (create/read/delete) with 100% success.
- Alerts: no new error-level alerts for 30m post-phase.

Rollbacks (fast path):
- If control plane becomes unstable: power off newly upgraded control-plane node(s) via BMC and rejoin previous stable control plane nodes if available.
- If worker regressions are severe: cordon + drain new nodes, and scale up previous AMI/image pool (or reprovision from stage snapshot).
- Terraform rollback pattern: keep previous statefile snapshot and a copy of the previous applied modules in the repo (tagged). Use a plan against the old module tag to revert.

Telemetry and SLOs to watch (minimum):
- Token metrics: kube-apiserver request latencies p50/p95/p99
- Kubelet heartbeats: node-heartbeat misses per minute
- Pod crashloop rate by pool
- Network retransmits and interface drops per NIC
- Registry pull failures (per-minute)
- Metric: control-plane availability (slo target 99.95% monthly for Dedicated/private deployments).

Common hardware/network gotchas we've encountered (field notes):
- Dell/Cumulus combos: some firmware combos require disabling LRO/GRO on host for stable kube-proxy hashing; otherwise cluster-level NAT breaks sporadically.
- vSphere: vSwitch security settings (promiscuous, forged transmits, MAC changes) must be set to accept during initial rollout then tightened after confirmation.
- Broadcom NICs: older drivers can mis-handle VLAN tags with VXLAN overlay; test with simple vxlan ping before CNI deploy.
- iDRAC IPMI: watch for duplicate BMC addresses from OEM provisioning images (we saw this twice).

Minimal commands for validation (copyable):
- etcd: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints="$(cat endpoints.txt)" endpoint status
- CNI test pod: kubectl run cni-test -n kube-system --rm --restart=Never --image=busybox --command -- sh -c "ping -c3 <other-pod-ip>"
- kubelet health: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep NotReady || true

Unresolved / TODOs (operational decisions to confirm per-customer):
- Decide whether to use metallb L2 vs L3 in customer topology with strict private VLANs. Default: L2 for simplicity unless routed load balancer needed.
- Define image retention policy for private registry (how long to keep old k8s images for rollback).
- Formalize firmware/driver matrix to gate automation.

Change log (high level):
- 2025-02-11: initial draft (Priya) with field resiliency patterns and TF interface sketch.
- 2025-03-10: added upgrade validation checks and more hardware gotcha entries (collab: Marta, Ethan).

Notes to self: keep this doc short for field techs. Move long-form troubleshooting to confluence (linked above).
